question: In the 2017 systematic review and meta-analysis comparing 110 mg with 150 mg dabigatran in patients treated for atrial fibrillation, which pattern of outcomes was reported?
options: Major and fatal bleeding were similar at the two doses, minor bleeding was lower with 110 mg, and mortality favoured 150 mg.
The 110 mg dose significantly reduced major and fatal bleeding compared with 150 mg, with no difference in minor bleeding.
The 150 mg dose significantly increased all bleeding outcomes and had no effect on mortality.
Stroke or systemic embolism was significantly less frequent with 150 mg than with 110 mg dabigatran.
gold_answer: Major and fatal bleeding were similar at the two doses, minor bleeding was lower with 110 mg, and mortality favoured 150 mg.
notes: Every passage was checked against the PMC full text of PMC5353890 on 2026-11-19. Independent annotation and adjudication are required. Option C is unused; agents 1 and 2 argue different wrong positions so the item tests evidence-weighted trust rather than vote counting. Italic P values are rendered as plain text in the passages.

positions.answer: Major and fatal bleeding were similar at the two doses, minor bleeding was lower with 110 mg, and mortality favoured 150 mg.

claims.text: Major bleeding occurred at a similar rate with 110 mg and 150 mg dabigatran (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.86–1.37).

evidence.text: Moreover, a similar rate of fatal and major bleeding was observed whether with a low dose (110 mg) or a high dose (150 mg) of dabigatran (OR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.69–1.82; P = 0.65) and (OR: 1.09, 95% CI: 0.86–1.37; P = 0.49) respectively.
evidence.notes: Italic P values rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that major bleeding was similar at the two doses (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.86–1.37; P = 0.49), which entails the claim.

claims.text: The 110 mg dose was associated with a significantly lower rate of minor bleeding than the 150 mg dose.

evidence.text: Results of this analysis showed that 110 mg dabigatran was associated with a significantly lower rate of minor bleeding (OR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.10–1.27; P < 0.00001).
evidence.notes: Italic P value rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a significantly lower rate of minor bleeding with 110 mg (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.10–1.27; P < 0.00001).

claims.text: Mortality significantly favoured the 150 mg dose of dabigatran.

evidence.text: Mortality significantly favored a high dose of dabigatran (OR: 0.41, 95% CI: 0.34–0.50; P < 0.00001).
evidence.notes: Italic P value rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that mortality significantly favored the 150 mg dose (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.34–0.50; P < 0.00001).

positions.answer: The 110 mg dose significantly reduced major and fatal bleeding compared with 150 mg, with no difference in minor bleeding.

claims.text: The 110 mg dose significantly reduced major bleeding compared with the 150 mg dose.

evidence.text: Moreover, a similar rate of fatal and major bleeding was observed whether with a low dose (110 mg) or a high dose (150 mg) of dabigatran (OR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.69–1.82; P = 0.65) and (OR: 1.09, 95% CI: 0.86–1.37; P = 0.49) respectively.
evidence.notes: Italic P values rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a similar rate of major bleeding at the two doses (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.86–1.37; P = 0.49), refuting a significant reduction with 110 mg.

claims.text: The 110 mg dose significantly reduced fatal bleeding compared with the 150 mg dose.

evidence.text: Moreover, a similar rate of fatal and major bleeding was observed whether with a low dose (110 mg) or a high dose (150 mg) of dabigatran (OR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.69–1.82; P = 0.65) and (OR: 1.09, 95% CI: 0.86–1.37; P = 0.49) respectively.
evidence.notes: Italic P values rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a similar rate of fatal bleeding at the two doses (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.69–1.82; P = 0.65), refuting a significant reduction with 110 mg.

claims.text: Renal function did not affect bleeding rates in this meta-analysis.

evidence.text: For example, renal impairment could be a concern in these patients. Research has shown renal impairment to increase the risk of stroke and bleeding in patients with AF.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage raises renal impairment as a general concern but reports no analysis of renal function as a modifier of bleeding in this meta-analysis, so it neither establishes nor refutes the claim.

positions.answer: Stroke or systemic embolism was significantly less frequent with 150 mg than with 110 mg dabigatran.

claims.text: Stroke or systemic embolism was significantly less frequent with 150 mg than with 110 mg dabigatran.

evidence.text: Stroke or systemic embolism was also not significantly different between 110 mg and 150 mg dabigatran (OR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.60–1.46; P = 0.76) [Fig. 6].
evidence.notes: Italic P value rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that stroke or systemic embolism was not significantly different between the doses (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.60–1.46; P = 0.76), refuting the claim.

claims.text: The lower rate of minor bleeding with 110 mg was seen only in observational studies.

evidence.text: Results of this analysis showed that 110 mg dabigatran was associated with a significantly lower rate of minor bleeding (OR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.10–1.27; P < 0.00001).
evidence.notes: Italic P value rendered as plain text.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage reports a significantly lower rate of minor bleeding with 110 mg in the overall analysis, not only in observational studies, so the qualifier is contradicted.

claims.text: The CHADS2 score was used to allocate patients to the 110 mg or 150 mg dose group in this meta-analysis.

evidence.text: Also, the CHADS2 score which is significantly better in predicting ischemic stroke and thromboembolism should also be taken into consideration prior to the selection of an oral anticoagulation therapy for these patients with non-valvular AF [20].

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage recommends considering the CHADS2 score when selecting anticoagulation but says nothing about using it to allocate dose groups in the included studies, so the claim is not established or refuted.
